draft.title: Primary and secondary sources
card: A source made during the time being studied, by someone who lived then. A tomb painting from ancient Egypt is one.
A source made later, about the time being studied. A modern textbook on ancient Egypt is one.
The same object can be either one. It depends on which time the historian is studying.
To decide, ask when the source was made. Compare that with the time being studied.
draft.remember: Primary or secondary depends on when a source was made, compared with the time studied.

a.q: Which of these is a primary source for the study of ancient Egypt?
opts: A statue carved in Egypt about 3,000 years ago
A museum website about Egyptian pharaohs
A film about Egypt made in the year 2000
A school textbook on Egyptian burial customs
a.why: The statue was made in ancient Egypt, during the time being studied. The other three were made much later, so they are secondary sources. The website may use real objects, but it was still made later.
a.clue: Which one was made while ancient Egypt existed?

b.q: Priya is studying life in Roman Britain. Which source is secondary for her topic?
opts: A history book written in 2015 about Roman Britain
A letter written by a Roman soldier in Britain
A coin made in Britain under Roman rule
A tombstone from Roman Britain with a carved name
b.why: The 2015 book was made long after Roman Britain, so it is secondary. The coin is tempting because it is old, but it was made during the time Priya studies, so it is primary.
b.clue: Compare when each source was made with the time studied.

a.best: A statue carved in Egypt about 3,000 years ago

b.best: A history book written in 2015 about Roman Britain
